messages.content: Predict this participant’s actual contribution in a one-shot public-goods field experiment in rural Kavango, northern Namibia. The four group members can identify each other. Each receives 10 experimental coins and privately allocates a whole number from 0 to 10 coins to the group, keeping the remainder. Group contributions are doubled and divided equally among all four members, including the contributor. Thus this person’s allocation earnings in coins are 10 minus their contribution plus one half of the total contribution of all four members. One experimental coin is worth 5 Namibian dollars (NAD); final cash amounts are rounded up to a whole NAD. There is no subsequent game round or punishment stage. Each person privately answered two comprehension questions and then estimated the average contribution of the OTHER THREE members, before making this allocation. An estimate judged correct earns a separate 20 NAD bonus; this does not depend on the estimator’s own contribution. Now the estimate is already submitted. Decisions use separate sealed envelopes for kept and contributed coins. Contributions and earnings are not revealed to group members before this choice; payment is private after the subsequent individual survey. Return only the whole number of experimental coins contributed, not NAD, a percentage, or a group total.
